title: Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning for Portfolio Management

problem.claim: Non-stationary financial markets with frequent regime shifts and structural changes make traditional portfolio management approaches ineffective.

gap.claim: Rolling-window retraining has high computational costs, while naive online fine-tuning has insufficient knowledge utilization, leading to low returns and limited adaptability.

contributions.claim: ReCAP integrates continual learning into portfolio management for dynamic financial environments.
ReCAP detects variable-length market regimes, learns regime-specific policy vectors, and constructs a policy library.
A regime-gate adaptively combines policy vectors based on the current market state, while continual updates are restricted to the gate and current regime policy vector.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe ReCAP as a novel framework integrating continual learning into portfolio management.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets reportedly show that ReCAP consistently outperforms popular baselines.
The authors report superior returns over long-term investment horizons and rapid adaptation to regime shifts.

narrative_sequence.summary: Financial market regime shifts undermine traditional portfolio management.
Existing retraining and fine-tuning remedies incur computational or knowledge-utilization limitations.
Continual learning can accumulate and transfer knowledge across sequential trading tasks.
ReCAP builds and adaptively combines regime-specific policy vectors, updating only selected components during continual trading.
The authors report favorable results across five real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework stores policy vectors for detected variable-length regimes and adaptively combines them according to the current market state.

interpretation.claim: Separating reusable regime-specific knowledge from a lightweight adaptation mechanism may support faster adjustment under distribution shift.

application.claim: In sequential decision systems with recurring or shifting conditions, maintain a reusable library of condition-specific policies and adaptively gate among them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the approach generalizes beyond the reported financial datasets or regime-detection setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the regime-detection method or gating mechanism.
The abstract does not report quantitative returns, baselines, datasets, trading costs, or statistical significance.
